recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No core spec follow-up is needed for this issue unless a future work group decision asks for a new language-specific validation rule or stronger conformance requirement.
issue_request: The Published FHIR-core STU3 issue requested automated enforcement of a banned list of reserved words for Java, C#, SQL, Javascript, and Delphi in extension names. The Not Persuasive with Modification resolution rejected a banned list as too broad and context-dependent, and instead called for a note warning that StructureDefinition.name and sliceName values used in code may collide with target-language reserved words and need code-generator handling.
initial_application: Git commit d26f97fdfc929858462f012cccd8520c21fb9488, matching Jira's svn 14560 comment through git-svn-id build@14560, applied GF#13880 by adding reserved-word collision notes to source/structuredefinition/structuredefinition-introduction.xml and source/downloads.html. Later edits preserved and polished the same warning.
additional_context: StructureDefinition is an active current resource in source/fhir.ini and downloads.html is listed in source/hierarchy.xml under Implementation Support. The current warning text covers names relevant for code generation, including structure names, element and slice names, codes, and target-language reserved words. Related Jira searches found only FHIR-13880, and issue-key Zulip plus Confluence reference searches found no directly relevant conflicting community record.
reconciliation: No source edit was made because the current source already implements the approved disposition: warn code generators about reserved-word collisions rather than enforcing a language-specific banned list.
